reason: Single-machine CPU+GPU pipeline fits the box, but data-cleaning semantics is a DB application rather than resource management and no repo is linked.
All-resource oversubscription is a textbook scheduling/resource-management problem replayable from public Azure traces, but the scout found no artifact at all.
GPU memory oversubscription and CPU-GPU work partitioning are systems-flavored and single-GPU by design; repo linked but completeness and dataset sizes unknown.

Openly released 2048-GPU LLM job trace enables trace-driven scheduling simulation on one host, but the artifact is trace+analysis only, so any improvement is simulator-side with no released baseline system.
Modular embedding-compression benchmark is a memory-footprint study with a real repo, but recommender datasets are large and the framing is ML-accuracy-heavy.
Conda-based scheduling simulator over device traces needs no cluster; resource-manager policy swaps are easy testable hypotheses, though the repo/paper naming mismatch adds mild risk.
User-space syscall services need no root, but the paper's Kata/KVM baselines are unreachable without /dev/kvm so the comparison space shrinks substantially.
Single-GPU DNN compiler with a Zenodo artifact, but the pinned CUDA/TVM stack against driver 535 is a real build risk and control-flow compilation is compiler rather than OS work.
Fuzzing is a testing/security tool rather than resource management, no artifact is public yet, and the LLM-guided loop needs API budget.
Cache partitioning in the PyTorch data loader is squarely caching+I/O with a named artifact, but 142 GB-1.4 TB datasets vs 257 GB free force a scale-down and one GPU limits job co-location.
Custom GPU decode kernels for a compressed weight format run on one GPU, but the headline trillion-parameter setting needs 3.2 TB of weights so the project must shrink to Switch base/large.
RoWild is a clean open user-space benchmark suite, but the paper is a characterization whose own conclusions argue for hardware changes and whose analysis leans on blocked perf counters.
Pageable B-Tree node layouts are ideal CPU-only storage-engine work with obvious layout/variant experiments, but no repo is linked which blocks the build-on requirement.
Explicit SSD access-pattern and cache-eviction design on one NVMe machine, but billion-scale datasets exceed the disk and no artifact was found.

CPU-only notebooks over public Alibaba/Azure/Google traces make reproduction trivial and the negative result invites an added downstream autoscaling evaluation; it is a short vision-track paper so the systems contribution is thin.
CPU-only model-based compression with outlier storage is real storage-engine work with a linked repo; compression-ratio/latency knobs give moderate but not rich headroom.
Entirely user-space Node/Chrome crawler, but web crawling is not an OS resource-management topic and the record-replay corpus plus nondeterminism make reproduction fiddly.
Learned SPN for approximate query answering is DB-modeling work far from OS concerns, with no repo located.

Self-contained Python tuner plus RocksDB harness runs comfortably here and LSM cost-model/solver swaps are crisp hypotheses, though the contribution is a learned tuner rather than a storage mechanism.
Query-engine-on-tensor-runtime is interesting compiler work but targets several XPU backends and no repo was located.
KV-cache sparsification plus quantization is core LLM memory management at 7B scale on one GPU, but the released code is mostly accuracy-side so end-to-end serving gains must be rewired by the team.

User-space CPU-only Wasm engine instrumentation is a runtime contribution, but the Virgil implementation language is an unusual toolchain and the topic is observability rather than resource management.
One GPU plus 16 CPU cores is exactly the paper's setting, the artifact is available, and preprocessing-stall policies offer clear incremental knobs.
User-space Ray runtime can be exercised with multiple local processes, but the evaluation assumes AWS clusters and serverless backends so results must be heavily scaled down.
Query-over-LLM operator optimization has no repo and depends on paid LLM API calls, making both build and evaluation unreliable here.
GNN cost model inside PostgreSQL trains on one GPU and has a repo, but learned query optimization is the anchor case for weak OS fit.
Cache-replacement traces are on-topic and CPU-only, but the contribution is LLM/RAG explanation rather than a policy mechanism, the repo ownership is unconfirmed, and API costs apply.
Symbolic verification of JIT transformations is PL/verification work, and the SpiderMonkey/Firefox integration is a heavy build for a 10-week budget.
DBMS knob tuning runs fine in user space with a linked repo, but ML-based configuration tuning sits well outside core OS resource management.
CUDA kernels behind torch.optim are single-GPU and the repo looks complete, but learned optimizers are an ML-training-method contribution rather than systems resource management.
Learned partitioning-key selection targets a distributed DBMS for end-to-end gains and has no released code.
Runs in user space but needs Gurobi plus a .NET toolchain, and the contribution is an optimization-encoding framework so improvements would be algorithmic rather than systems-performance.

Trace-driven single-machine serverless worker with strong memory/cold-start claims, but only the mmu backend is usable without KVM and the exec-mounted /dev/shm requirement needs a root-free workaround.
Runs on plain Linux with cgroup v2 delegation and trains its model on one GPU; main caveat is that memory-bandwidth contention fidelity is hard to measure without hardware counters.
User-space wasm-sandboxed LLM serving at model sizes that fit 24 GB, with new KV-cache strategies named by the authors as the extension point; only needs a user-space Rust toolchain.
Released disk-resident evaluation harness comparing learned indexes to B+-trees on NVMe is an ideal reproduce-and-extend target for this machine.
Temporal storage inside a graph DB is genuine storage-engine work with a repo and conda-installable JVM, but it is narrow and graph-specific.
KV-cache offloading with speculative prefetch is designed for exactly one GPU plus large host DRAM; 24 GB + 125 GiB and no root needed, with obvious prefetch/eviction policy variants.
Open single-node orchestration platform for continuous training; solid artifact but the contribution is pipeline orchestration rather than a resource-management mechanism.
Pure user-space concurrency contribution that a 32-thread machine exercises well, with an open artifact and obvious per-operation lock-policy variants to test.
Adaptive KV caching with recompute-vs-memory trade-off is a perfect single-GPU topic, but no code was found so there is nothing to build upon.
Pure user-space compiler/runtime with crisp graph-completeness and speedup metrics against TorchDynamo, but guard design is compiler work rather than OS resource management.
In-memory dynamic graph structure fits 125 GiB easily with a linked repo, but the space/throughput result is narrow and graph-specific.
Tokenizer-as-symbol-table is a neat encoding idea, but it is implemented inside closed-source Umbra so only a partial token-table artifact is reproducible.
Offline training/eval on a released Zenodo dataset means no edge fleet is needed, but the contribution is a prediction model whose systems payoff is not evaluated here.

LSM erasure-coding tiering is prime storage work with a real artifact, but the appendix asks for eight networked machines; co-locating 6-8 Cassandra JVMs preserves only the storage-savings claim, not latency/throughput.
SIMD and memory-access optimization for HNSW construction is CPU-only and fits perfectly, but ANN index building is closer to a data-structure kernel than OS resource management.
Changing degree of parallelism mid-query is a real scheduling mechanism with a repo, but it is built on Presto which normally needs a distributed deployment.
Spark AQE parameter tuning runs local/pseudo-distributed, but multi-objective ML tuning of a query engine is far from OS resource management and Spark local mode weakens the result.
Prefix-shared decode kernel with workload balancing runs on Ampere without FP8 and is directly comparable to FlashDecoding; repo linked but artifact completeness is unverified.
Explicitly a CPU-only, root-free virtual-memory research platform built to be extended - the ideal shape for a 10-week OS improvement project on this machine.
Weight deduplication is storage-relevant and single-GPU, but no repo was found and much of the contribution is privacy analysis.
No artifact URL, the DSL appears to assume Hopper-class tensor-core/TMA instructions rather than sm_86, and reproducing the agent loop costs LLM API budget.
LLM-inference simulator lets schedulers, batching and parallelism be studied without a cluster, with released profiling data; only local re-profiling on the A5000 is needed for validation.
Learned index inside LSM compaction is a good storage-engine topic for this machine, but no repo was located.
CPU work-stealing plus workload-aware GPU batching is genuine single-machine scheduling, but no artifact was found.
Hotness-aware KV-cache scheduling for prefix sharing is exactly the target topic, but the scout found neither abstract nor repo so nothing can be built on.
PostgreSQL + LibTorch extension for model storage and batched inference fits one GPU with a linked repo, but in-DB ML management is systems-adjacent at best.
BLADE plus Kernel Tuner run in user space, but the contribution is LLM-synthesized search algorithms, the paper sweeps six platforms where only one GPU exists, and generation needs API budget.
A tunable memory/throughput knob in a time-series ingestion engine is a good single-node storage topic, but no artifact was found.

Admission, eviction, quota and page-affinity policies on one NVMe disk are exactly the caching topic and trace-drivable, but it is a deployed-systems experience report whose mapping onto Alluxio's open-source cache must be verified.
Radix vertex index plus snapshot-log edge storage is an in-memory structure with an open artifact that fits easily, but it is graph-specific rather than general storage.
Single-node Java/C++ artifact runs fine, but RL-based join attribute ordering is query-optimizer ML, the weakest OS-fit category.
Fully badged AE artifact (Available/Functional/Reproduced) for single-GPU sparse LLM inference; the A100/4090 tuning constants needing revisit on SM86 is itself a ready-made improvement hypothesis.
Actor scheduling and reference-based intermediate storage can run as multiple processes on one host, but the system is designed for a cluster so the headline results will not transfer cleanly.
Pure single-GPU sparse kernel work, but the artifact branch is Docker-based (unavailable here) and was tuned for A100, so a user-space rebuild plus retuning is required before any improvement.
Pure user-space Java concurrency library with JMH microbenchmarks on a 32-thread machine and no root/GPU needs; only concern is that the original scalability curves come from a wider machine.

The paper's own evaluation is a single consumer GPU with CPU-side residuals over PCIe on 3-4 bit 8B models, an exact match; artifact quality is unverified and Ada-specific kernel assumptions need checking.
User-space single-GPU tooling with a repo, but it is a debugging sanitizer rather than resource management and the AE scripts assume a ROCm Docker image that must be ported.
Learned index plus RL parameter tuner integrated into RocksDB runs on one node and offers many policy/knob ablations, but the learned-component framing dilutes the OS angle.
Released harness makes a careful reproduction straightforward, but learned query optimization is the anchor example of weak OS fit and the paper is already a re-evaluation.
CPU-GPU-IO pipelined MoE offloading evaluated on a 16 GB T4 reproduces directly on a 24 GB A5000, and the pipeline/scheduling policy is an obvious place for incremental improvement.
CPU-only single-machine reproduction repo, but filtered vector search is an indexing algorithm rather than a systems resource-management problem.

Unified buffer pool and memory allocation across concurrent larger-than-memory joins in DuckDB is real user-space memory management that fits 125 GiB; the repo is an experiments repo so DuckDB-side integration must be checked.
Wasm self-decoding dataset format with DuckDB integration is user-space storage work and Rust/wasm install in $HOME; the Spark path and decode-overhead claims need scaled-down data.
Single-GPU sparse-convolution kernel work with released code, but it is a domain-specific ML kernel and the datasets are large with an older CUDA target.
Scheduling-based determinism via verified speculation runs on one GPU with a 7-8B model and has an official Microsoft repo; the scheduling/verification trade-off is a rich space of testable variants.
A user-space concurrency library would run perfectly on 32 threads, but no repo was located so there is nothing to extend.

vLLM cold start is characterized as a CPU-bound six-step process on one GPU with released benchmark scripts and an analytical model, so cutting or predicting startup latency is directly testable here.

The transformation-reordering half is a single-node tf.data question that tests cleanly here, but the hybrid-placement half assumes disaggregated remote CPU workers and cloud VMs/TPUs that cannot be reproduced.
